rv.q: Galileo at the Trap Door Theatre is a brilliant feast for the mind and soul; the concept so masterfully realized it is three-dimensional poetry manifested.
Max Truax and his cast have fashioned a seamless, horrifying analog to daily lived experience.
Under resident director Max Truax, Trap Door offers a brilliant interpretation of this play—intelligent, gutsy and moving.

Trap Door’s Galileo points out our own Inquisition Angela Allyn May 9, 2025 2 min read I am absolutely certain that when Trap Door Theatre set its season last year they had no idea the kind of anti scientific underworld we would be living in when Brecht’s WW2 era script would be brought thrillingly to stage by Brechtian master Max Truax.
Lovejoy’s performance is intense, and a remarkable achievement overall: and he is on stage every minute of the two hour show.
I was fascinated by the production and its way of framing science’s struggles.
Trap Door Theatre's presentation of “Galileo” stays close to the heart of Bertolt Brecht’s script but is a challenging and thought-provoking interpretation.

cn.t: Critics praise this bold, timely Trap Door production for its masterful Brechtian staging and striking visual design. David Lovejoy's performance and Max Truax's postmodern direction earn acclaim for making the 1938 play resonate powerfully today.
